GitHub Brach : UI-UX/-Create-profile-page-v1

1. Shared Understanding

Goal

Create a Profile page where signed-in users can manage their personal account details, subscription status, password, and GoThru dashboard connection from the same workspace experience used by the product-docs dashboard.

Product Intent

The page should feel like a natural sibling of the Workspace dashboard, not a separate settings product. It should keep the same MapThru shell, left navigation, ambient brand depth, rounded workspace cards, and calm account-management tone.

In Scope

  • Profile summary and edit area.
  • Upload avatar.
  • Delete avatar.
  • Edit full name.
  • Display email as read-only because it cannot be changed.
  • Show subscription plan information.
  • Show Upgrade to Pro when the user has no active subscription.
  • Show Manage subscription when the user has an active subscription.
  • Show clear past due and canceled plan states.
  • Reset password for manual registration users:
    • Old password.
    • New password.
    • Confirm new password.
  • Set a new password for Google OAuth users:
    • New password.
    • Confirm new password.
  • Connect GoThru dashboard.
  • Disconnect GoThru dashboard.
  • Loading, success, empty, and error states for all account actions.
  • Non-technical page copy and design direction.

Out of Scope

  • Changing email address.
  • Deleting the account.
  • Building a full multi-page settings center.
  • Team or organization management.
  • Invoice history.
  • Notification preferences.
  • Developer settings.
  • API key management.
  • Detailed Pro feature comparison.

2. Dashboard Style Source of Truth

The profile page must be based on the dashboard style from the product-docs branch.

Shell Pattern

Use the same overall workspace shell:

  • Full-page background using the app background color.
  • Soft ambient brand wash behind the content.
  • Sticky top MapThru navigation.
  • Left sidebar on large screens.
  • Center content area.
  • Optional right rail for contextual account status or upgrade prompt.
  • Wide max-width workspace container.
  • Responsive stacking on smaller screens.

Navigation Pattern

Use the existing dashboard navigation model:

  • Top nav contains MapThru branding and the account popover.
  • Left sidebar contains account/workspace links.
  • Profile is a first-class sidebar item.
  • On the Profile page, the Profile item should be active.
  • Workspace remains available as the route back to projects.

Visual Language

Preserve these dashboard cues:

  • Rounded-xl and rounded-2xl surfaces.
  • Subtle borders using low-contrast border color.
  • Semi-transparent card backgrounds.
  • Backdrop blur where the dashboard uses glass-like depth.
  • Small icon-led labels.
  • Muted helper text.
  • Gradient primary action for the main action on the page.
  • Primary color accents for active states.
  • Amber treatment for upgrade or billing attention.
  • Destructive styling only for delete, disconnect, or failed states.
  • Concise page title treatment similar to Workspace.

What Not to Copy

Do not turn Profile into another project list. The style should match the dashboard, but the content should remain account-focused. Avoid a marketing hero, large plan comparison, decorative-only cards, or nested card stacks.

3. Recommended Page Direction

Recommended Approach: Account Page Inside Dashboard Shell

Build the Profile page as a dedicated /profile workspace page:

  1. Keep the dashboard shell and top navigation.
  2. Keep the left sidebar with Profile active.
  3. Use the center column for profile, password, and connection cards.
  4. Use the right rail for a compact subscription or GoThru connection summary.
  5. Keep all copy short and user-facing.

This is the best fit because the product-docs dashboard already frames Profile as part of the workspace navigation. Users should not feel they have entered a different app when managing their account.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative A: Centered standalone profile form

This would be simple, but it would not honor the product-docs dashboard direction. It would feel closer to the current Billing page than the newer Workspace dashboard.

Alternative B: Tabbed settings page

This would scale to many future settings, but it is too heavy for the current feature. The requested page has a clear and limited account scope.

Alternative C: Profile popover only

This would make common actions fast, but avatar, password, subscription, and connection management need more room than a popover should hold.

4. Page Layout

Overall Layout

The page should follow this structure:

  1. Sticky top MapThru nav.
  2. Workspace container with three zones:
    • Left sidebar navigation.
    • Main profile content.
    • Right contextual rail on wide screens.
  3. Mobile and tablet views stack the content, with sidebar navigation adapting to the existing dashboard behavior.

Header Area

Purpose: Tell the user where they are and which account they are editing.

Content:

  • Small account context row, similar to the dashboard greeting row.
  • Main title: Profile.
  • Supporting line: Manage your account, plan, security, and GoThru connection.
  • Primary action: Save changes, only when there are unsaved profile edits.

Style:

  • Use the same title scale and gradient text treatment as Workspace, adjusted for Profile.
  • Keep the header compact.
  • Do not use a marketing hero.

Main Column

Recommended order:

  1. Profile information card.
  2. Subscription plan card.
  3. Password and security card.
  4. GoThru dashboard connection card.

The order starts with identity, then plan, then security, then external connection. This matches the most common user mental model: who I am, what I have, how I sign in, what I am connected to.

Right Rail

On wide screens, use the right rail for a small contextual summary:

  • If user is Free or inactive: Upgrade to Pro prompt using the dashboard's amber upgrade treatment.
  • If user is Pro: Plan status summary.
  • If GoThru dashboard is disconnected: Connect prompt.
  • If GoThru dashboard is connected: Connected account summary.

The right rail should support the main content, not duplicate every form control.

5. Profile Information Card

Purpose

Let users review and update their visible account identity.

Content

  • Avatar preview.
  • Upload avatar button.
  • Delete avatar button when an avatar exists.
  • Full name field.
  • Email display.
  • Read-only email helper text.
  • Save changes action.

States

No avatar

  • Show initials in a circular avatar, matching the dashboard account popover.
  • Offer Upload avatar.

Avatar exists

  • Show avatar image.
  • Offer Upload avatar and Delete avatar.

Editing full name

  • Save action becomes available.
  • If the name is empty, show validation before saving.

Email

  • Email is always displayed as read-only information.
  • It should not look like a normal editable field.
  • Helper text: Email cannot be changed.

Suggested Copy

  • Card title: Profile information
  • Full name label: Full name
  • Email label: Email
  • Email helper: Email cannot be changed.
  • Upload button: Upload avatar
  • Delete button: Delete avatar
  • Save button: Save changes
  • Loading: Saving profile...
  • Success: Profile updated.
  • Error: We could not update your profile. Please try again.

6. Subscription Plan Card

Purpose

Show current plan status and give the correct next action.

Free or Inactive State

Content:

  • Plan label: Free.
  • Short explanation that Pro unlocks more capability.
  • Upgrade to Pro button.

Suggested copy:

  • You are currently on the Free plan.
  • Upgrade to Pro to unlock more MapThru workspace features.
  • Upgrade to Pro

Active Pro State

Content:

  • Plan label: Pro.
  • Active status.
  • Renewal or period end date if available.
  • Manage subscription button.

Suggested copy:

  • Your Pro subscription is active.
  • Renews on [date].
  • Manage subscription

Past Due State

Content:

  • Clear warning message.
  • Button to manage subscription.

Suggested copy:

  • Your subscription payment is past due.
  • Manage subscription

Canceled State

Content:

  • Clear canceled message.
  • Button to upgrade or resubscribe.

Suggested copy:

  • Your subscription has been canceled.
  • Upgrade to Pro

Style Notes

  • Use amber visual treatment for upgrade, payment attention, and plan prompts.
  • Avoid a full pricing table.
  • Keep the card compact like the dashboard's right-side Upgrade to Pro prompt.

7. Password and Security Card

Purpose

Show the correct password form based on the user's registration method.

Manual Registration State

Show a reset password form:

  • Old password.
  • New password.
  • Confirm new password.
  • Update password button.

Suggested helper text:

  • Change the password used for email sign-in.

Google OAuth State

Show a set password form:

  • New password.
  • Confirm new password.
  • Set password button.

Suggested helper text:

  • Set a password if you also want to sign in with email.

Unknown Account Type State

If the app cannot determine whether the user registered manually or through Google OAuth, do not show the wrong form. Show a calm message:

  • We could not confirm which password options are available for this account. Please try again later.

Validation

  • New password and confirm new password must match.
  • Old password is required for manual users.
  • New password must meet product password rules.
  • Show errors close to the related fields.
  • Do not clear fields until the action succeeds.

Suggested Copy

  • Card title: Password and security
  • Old password
  • New password
  • Confirm new password
  • Update password
  • Set password
  • Password updated.
  • New password and confirmation do not match.
  • Enter your current password.
  • We could not update your password. Please try again.

8. GoThru Dashboard Connection Card

Purpose

Let users connect or disconnect their GoThru dashboard account from the MapThru workspace.

Disconnected State

Content:

  • Status: Not connected.
  • Short explanation.
  • Connect GoThru dashboard button.

Suggested copy:

  • Connect your GoThru dashboard to use linked GoThru services from this workspace.
  • Connect GoThru dashboard

Connected State

Content:

  • Status: Connected.
  • Connected account name or email when available.
  • Disconnect button.

Suggested copy:

  • Connected to [account].
  • Disconnect

Working State

  • Connect button becomes Connecting...
  • Disconnect button becomes Disconnecting...
  • Prevent duplicate clicks.

Failure State

Suggested copy:

  • We could not update the GoThru dashboard connection. Please try again.

Style Notes

  • Use the Plug-style connection language already present in the dashboard account popover.
  • Connect should look like a primary or strong secondary action.
  • Disconnect should be visually quieter than delete but still clearly cautionary.
  • Consider a lightweight confirmation before disconnecting.

9. Key User Flows

Flow A: Update Profile

  1. User opens Profile from the dashboard sidebar or account popover.
  2. Profile page opens in the dashboard shell.
  3. User uploads or deletes avatar.
  4. User edits full name.
  5. User sees email but understands it cannot be changed.
  6. User saves changes.
  7. Page confirms the profile was updated.

Flow B: Upgrade to Pro

  1. User opens Profile.
  2. Subscription card shows Free plan.
  3. User clicks Upgrade to Pro.
  4. User moves into checkout.
  5. After successful subscription, Profile shows Pro active.

Flow C: Manage Pro Subscription

  1. User opens Profile.
  2. Subscription card shows Pro active.
  3. User clicks Manage subscription.
  4. User moves into the subscription management flow.

Flow D: Manual User Updates Password

  1. User opens Profile.
  2. Password card shows old password, new password, and confirm fields.
  3. User fills all fields.
  4. User clicks Update password.
  5. Page confirms the password was updated.

Flow E: Google OAuth User Sets Password

  1. User opens Profile.
  2. Password card explains that email sign-in can be enabled by setting a password.
  3. User enters new password and confirmation.
  4. User clicks Set password.
  5. Page confirms the password was set.

Flow F: Connect GoThru Dashboard

  1. User opens Profile.
  2. GoThru dashboard card shows Not connected.
  3. User clicks Connect GoThru dashboard.
  4. User completes the connection step.
  5. Profile returns with Connected status.

Flow G: Disconnect GoThru Dashboard

  1. User opens Profile.
  2. GoThru dashboard card shows Connected.
  3. User clicks Disconnect.
  4. User confirms if confirmation is required.
  5. Profile returns with Not connected status.

10. States and Edge Cases

Loading States

  • Loading profile information.
  • Saving profile.
  • Uploading avatar.
  • Deleting avatar.
  • Loading subscription.
  • Starting upgrade.
  • Opening subscription management.
  • Updating password.
  • Setting password.
  • Connecting GoThru dashboard.
  • Disconnecting GoThru dashboard.

Empty States

  • No avatar: show initials.
  • No full name: use email as account identity.
  • No subscription: show Free plan and Upgrade to Pro.
  • No GoThru dashboard connection: show Not connected.

Error States

  • Profile information cannot load.
  • Avatar upload fails.
  • Avatar delete fails.
  • Full name save fails.
  • Subscription status cannot load.
  • Upgrade or subscription management cannot start.
  • Password fields are incomplete.
  • Password confirmation does not match.
  • Password update fails.
  • GoThru dashboard connect fails.
  • GoThru dashboard disconnect fails.

Edge Cases

  • User has a long name.
  • User has a long email.
  • User has an unverified email.
  • User has no avatar.
  • User is Free.
  • User is Pro.
  • User has past due billing.
  • User has canceled billing.
  • User registered manually.
  • User registered with Google OAuth.
  • User registered with Google OAuth and later set a password.
  • User's GoThru dashboard connection status is temporarily unavailable.

11. Accessibility and Usability

  • Every editable field has a visible label.
  • Email is visibly read-only and not styled like a normal editable input.
  • Buttons have clear action labels.
  • Avatar upload and delete controls are keyboard reachable.
  • Password errors appear near the fields they affect.
  • Success and error messages do not rely on color alone.
  • Focus order follows the visual card order.
  • The active Profile sidebar item is announced as the current page.
  • Destructive or cautionary actions use clear labels.
  • Text fits in cards on smaller screens.
  • Long account names and emails truncate gracefully where needed.

12. Acceptance Criteria

Layout and Style

  • Profile page uses the same shell as the product-docs dashboard.
  • Top MapThru nav is present.
  • Left sidebar is present on large screens.
  • Profile is the active sidebar item.
  • Main content uses dashboard-style rounded cards and muted helper text.
  • Ambient brand wash and workspace depth feel consistent with the dashboard.
  • The page does not use a standalone centered settings layout.

Profile Information

  • User can see avatar, full name, and email.
  • User can upload an avatar.
  • User can delete an existing avatar.
  • User can edit full name.
  • User cannot edit email.
  • User sees a clear explanation that email cannot be changed.
  • User sees success after profile changes.
  • User sees helpful errors when profile changes fail.

Subscription

  • User can see current plan.
  • Free or inactive users see Upgrade to Pro.
  • Active Pro users see Manage subscription.
  • Past due users see a past due message.
  • Canceled users see a canceled message.
  • Loading and error states are visible.

Password

  • Manual users see old password, new password, and confirm new password.
  • Google OAuth users see new password and confirm new password only.
  • Mismatched password confirmation shows an error.
  • Successful password update or setup is confirmed.
  • Failed password update or setup shows a helpful error.

GoThru Dashboard Connection

  • Disconnected users see Connect GoThru dashboard.
  • Connected users see Disconnect.
  • Current connection state is visible.
  • Connect and disconnect actions show progress.
  • Success and failure messages are visible.

13. Suggested UI Copy

Header

  • Profile
  • Manage your account, plan, security, and GoThru connection.

Profile Information

  • Profile information
  • Upload avatar
  • Delete avatar
  • Full name
  • Email
  • Email cannot be changed.
  • Save changes
  • Profile updated.

Subscription

  • Subscription plan
  • You are currently on the Free plan.
  • Your Pro subscription is active.
  • Your subscription payment is past due.
  • Your subscription has been canceled.
  • Upgrade to Pro
  • Manage subscription

Password

  • Password and security
  • Change the password used for email sign-in.
  • Set a password if you also want to sign in with email.
  • Old password
  • New password
  • Confirm new password
  • Update password
  • Set password
  • Password updated.

GoThru Dashboard

  • GoThru dashboard
  • Connected
  • Not connected
  • Connect GoThru dashboard
  • Disconnect
  • GoThru dashboard connected.
  • GoThru dashboard disconnected.

14. QA Scenarios

  1. User opens Profile from the sidebar and sees the Profile sidebar item active.
  2. User with no avatar sees initials in the avatar area.
  3. User uploads a valid avatar and sees the preview update.
  4. User deletes avatar and sees initials return.
  5. User edits full name and saves successfully.
  6. User sees email as read-only and cannot edit it.
  7. Free user sees Upgrade to Pro.
  8. Pro user sees Manage subscription.
  9. Past due user sees a past due subscription message.
  10. Manual user sees old password, new password, and confirm fields.
  11. Google OAuth user sees only new password and confirm fields.
  12. Password mismatch shows an error.
  13. Disconnected user can start GoThru dashboard connection.
  14. Connected user can disconnect GoThru dashboard.
  15. Profile page remains usable with keyboard-only navigation.
  16. Long names and emails do not break the layout.

15. Open Questions

Question Recommended default Owner
Should Profile also be linked from the account popover? Yes, replace or activate the current Settings placeholder with Profile when ready. Product / Design
Should disconnecting GoThru dashboard require confirmation? Yes, use a lightweight confirmation because it removes a connection. Product
What avatar formats and size limits are allowed? Allow common image formats and show a clear unsupported-file error. Product / Engineering
What Pro benefits should appear in the small upgrade prompt? Keep it short; mention only the top one or two benefits. Product
What connected GoThru identity should be shown? Show connected account name or email if available. Product / Engineering
Should unverified email appear on Profile too? Yes, mirror the dashboard email verification alert in a smaller account context. Product
How should Google OAuth users who already set a password be treated? Show the manual password update form after a password exists. Product / Engineering

16. Risks

Risk Impact Mitigation
Profile page drifts away from the product-docs dashboard style. The app feels inconsistent. Reuse the dashboard shell, sidebar, card rhythm, and account popover patterns.
Page becomes too dense. Users miss important account actions. Keep cards short and use the right rail only for summaries.
Wrong password form appears for the account type. User confusion and failed updates. Treat account type as a required page state.
Email looks editable even though it is not. Users repeatedly try to change it. Style email as read-only information with explicit helper text.
GoThru dashboard connection value is unclear. Users may ignore the connection action. Explain the benefit in one plain sentence.
Subscription copy conflicts with billing page copy. Users may distrust plan status. Reuse the same plan state language where possible.

17. Design Summary

The Profile page should be a dashboard-native account page. It should keep the product-docs branch workspace shell, activate Profile in the sidebar, and organize account tasks into clear rounded cards. The user should immediately understand: who they are signed in as, whether their profile is complete, what plan they are on, how they manage their password, and whether their GoThru dashboard is connected.

brainstorming.md - Billing Page

Branch: product-docs
Brainstorming File: docs\superpowers\specs\2026-07-02-billing-page-brainstorming.md

RESULT

GitHub Brach : UI-UX-Create-billing-page

1. Shared Understanding

Goal

Create a Billing page where users can view, add, and edit billing information for MapThru. The page should support billing address details, saved payment method information, tax guidance, and country-specific payment behavior.

Product Intent

Billing should feel like part of the MapThru workspace, not a detached checkout form. The page should use the same dashboard style: MapThru top navigation, left sidebar, soft ambient background, rounded cards, muted helper text, clear section labels, and a right-side summary area on wide screens.

In Scope

  • Billing address form.
  • Billing contact details.
  • Company and tax details.
  • Card information area.
  • Clear explanation that MapThru does not store card details.
  • Stripe security message for payment information.
  • Saved card display after a user subscribes or purchases through Stripe.
  • Canada tax information by province or territory.
  • India one-time-payment or no-renewal-payment information.
  • Field priority recommendations: mandatory, optional, important, and not important.
  • Loading, saved, empty, validation, and error states.
  • Non-technical English suitable for product and design planning.

Out of Scope

  • Invoice history.
  • Receipts download.
  • Refund management.
  • Coupon management.
  • Plan comparison.
  • Full checkout flow.
  • Tax filing advice.
  • Manual card storage inside MapThru.
  • Editing raw Stripe customer settings inside MapThru.

2. Dashboard Style Source of Truth

The Billing page should be based on the style of src/app/dashboard/page.tsx.

Shell Pattern

Use the same workspace shell:

  • Full-page app background.
  • Soft ambient brand wash behind the content.
  • Sticky MapThru top navigation.
  • Left sidebar on large screens.
  • Center content area.
  • Right information rail on wide screens.
  • Wide workspace container with comfortable spacing.
  • Responsive stacking on smaller screens.

Visual Language

Preserve these dashboard cues:

  • Rounded-xl and rounded-2xl surfaces.
  • Soft borders.
  • Semi-transparent card backgrounds.
  • Muted helper text.
  • Small icon-led labels.
  • Primary color accents for active and saved states.
  • Amber treatment for tax, billing attention, or payment notices.
  • Destructive styling only for failed or risky actions.
  • Compact headings.
  • Gradient primary action for the main save action.

Navigation Pattern

  • Billing should be a first-class sidebar page.
  • The Billing sidebar item should be active on this page.
  • Workspace remains available as the route back to projects.
  • The page should not use the old centered billing-card layout.

3. Recommended Page Direction

Recommended Approach: Billing Settings Inside the Dashboard Shell

Use a dedicated Billing page with:

  1. A dashboard-style header.
  2. A main column for editable billing details.
  3. A secure payment method card.
  4. A country-aware tax information card.
  5. A right rail with payment status and short security messaging.

This approach is recommended because billing is an account-management task. Users should be able to review and edit billing data without feeling like they have entered a separate checkout flow.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative A: Checkout-style billing page

This would make payment entry feel direct, but it would over-focus on payment and under-serve billing address maintenance.

Alternative B: One long form

This would be simple to build, but it would feel dense and easy to abandon. Users need clear sections for address, tax, and payment.

Alternative C: Billing data hidden inside a modal

This would keep the page small, but billing information is important enough to deserve a full workspace page.

4. Page Layout

Header Area

Purpose: Tell the user what the page manages.

Suggested content:

  • Small context label: Account billing
  • Main title: Billing
  • Supporting text: Manage your billing address, tax details, and payment method.
  • Main action: Save billing details

Style:

  • Use the same title treatment as the dashboard.
  • Keep the header compact.
  • Do not create a marketing hero.

Main Column

Recommended order:

  1. Billing address card.
  2. Tax details card.
  3. Payment method card.
  4. Country-specific payment notice card.

Right Rail

On wide screens, show a compact summary:

  • Billing profile status: Complete or incomplete.
  • Payment method status: No card, card on file, or managed by Stripe.
  • Tax note based on selected country.
  • Security note: Card information is handled securely by Stripe.

The right rail should summarize, not duplicate the full form.

5. Billing Address Card

Purpose

Collect the information needed to create invoices, calculate taxes, and identify the billing contact.

Fields

  • First name.
  • Last name.
  • Billing email.
  • Company name.
  • Address.
  • Address line 2.
  • City.
  • Country.
  • State or province.
  • ZIP or postal code.
  • Phone number.

Behavior

  • Billing email can default to the account email but should remain editable for billing communication.
  • Country controls which state/province options appear.
  • State/province should be required when the selected country needs it for taxes.
  • ZIP/postal code label should adapt to the country where possible.
  • The page should clearly show which fields are required.

Suggested Copy

  • Card title: Billing address
  • Helper text: Used for invoices, tax calculation, and billing communication.
  • Save success: Billing details saved.
  • Save error: We could not save your billing details. Please try again.

6. Tax Details Card

Purpose

Collect optional tax information and explain country-specific tax behavior in plain language.

Fields

  • Tax number.
  • Company name, if not already entered in the billing address card.
  • Country.
  • State or province.

Canada Tax Display

When the user selects Canada, show tax information based on the selected province or territory. Use the user's selected province or territory to display the estimated tax rate before purchase or renewal.

Recommended Canada tax table:

Province or territory Tax display
Alberta 5% GST
British Columbia 5% GST + 7% PST = 12%
Manitoba 5% GST + 7% PST = 12%
New Brunswick 15% HST
Newfoundland and Labrador 15% HST
Northwest Territories 5% GST
Nova Scotia 14% HST
Nunavut 5% GST
Ontario 13% HST
Prince Edward Island 15% HST
Quebec 5% GST + 9.975% QST = 14.975%
Saskatchewan 5% GST + 6% PST = 11%
Yukon 5% GST

Plain-language note:

  • Canadian taxes are estimated from the selected billing province or territory. Final tax may depend on the place of supply, the type of purchase, and Stripe tax settings.

India Payment Note

When the user selects India, show a clear payment notice:

  • For India billing addresses, MapThru should use a one-time payment or no-renewal payment flow. The user should not see an automatic renewal promise unless the payment setup supports it for India.

Suggested copy:

  • India billing notice: For India billing addresses, this purchase is treated as a one-time payment with no automatic renewal unless a supported renewal flow is shown.

Suggested Copy

  • Card title: Tax details
  • Helper text: Tax details help MapThru prepare accurate invoices.
  • Tax number label: Tax number
  • Canada note: Tax is estimated from your selected province or territory.
  • India note: India payments may be one-time or non-renewing.

7. Payment Method Card

Purpose

Show card information after the user subscribes or purchases through Stripe, and let the user add or update a payment method safely.

Important Security Message

MapThru does not store full card information. Card details are collected and stored securely by Stripe. MapThru may only show safe card details such as card brand, last four digits, and expiration date after Stripe returns them.

Empty State

Show when the user has not subscribed or purchased yet:

  • No payment method yet.
  • Card information will appear after you subscribe or make a purchase with Stripe.
  • Add payment method or Subscribe, depending on the page goal.

Card on File State

Show after Stripe has a payment method:

  • Card brand.
  • Last four digits.
  • Expiration date.
  • Name on card, if available.
  • Button to update payment method.

Do not show:

  • Full card number.
  • Security code.
  • Raw card data.

Add or Update Card Form

When adding or updating card information, the visible fields should be:

  • Card number.
  • Expiration date.
  • Security code.
  • Name on card.

The form should make it clear that these fields are handled securely through Stripe.

Suggested Copy

  • Card title: Payment method
  • Empty state: Card information will appear after you subscribe or purchase through Stripe.
  • Security note: MapThru does not store your card details. Card information is handled securely by Stripe.
  • Saved card: Card ending in [last four digits].
  • Update button: Update payment method
  • Add button: Add payment method
  • Loading: Loading payment method...
  • Error: We could not load your payment method. Please try again.

8. Field Priority Recommendations

Mandatory Fields

These fields should be required because they are needed for billing identity, tax calculation, invoices, or payment:

Field Why it is mandatory
First name Identifies the billing contact.
Last name Identifies the billing contact.
Billing email Sends billing updates, receipts, and payment notices.
Address Required for billing records and tax calculation.
City Required for billing records and tax calculation.
Country Required for tax, payment rules, and address format.
State or province Required when the country uses it for tax or address rules.
ZIP or postal code Required for billing records, tax, and card verification.
Card number Required only when adding or updating a payment method.
Expiration date Required only when adding or updating a payment method.
Security code Required only when adding or updating a payment method.
Name on card Required only when adding or updating a payment method.

Optional but Important Fields

These fields should be optional, but the page should encourage users to fill them when relevant:

Field Why it is important
Company name Useful for business invoices.
Phone number Helpful for billing follow-up or payment issues.
Tax number Important for businesses that need tax-compliant invoices.
Address line 2 Useful for apartment, suite, unit, or building details.

Optional and Less Important Fields

These fields are not critical for most users:

Field Why it is less important
Company name for personal users Personal users may not have a company.
Phone number for low-risk accounts Email is usually enough for normal billing communication.
Tax number for personal users Personal users usually do not need a tax number on invoices.

Recommended Field Treatment

  • Mark mandatory fields with a clear required indicator.
  • Do not overload the form with too many required fields.
  • Keep optional fields visible but visually calmer.
  • For business users, make company name and tax number feel important without blocking save.
  • For personal users, let them skip company and tax details easily.

9. Country-Specific Behavior

Canada

When Country is Canada:

  • State/province becomes mandatory.
  • Show a province or territory selector.
  • Show the estimated tax rate after province or territory is selected.
  • Show a plain note that final tax may depend on Stripe and the final purchase details.

Example:

  • Country: Canada
  • Province: Ontario
  • Tax note: Estimated tax: 13% HST.

India

When Country is India:

  • Show a payment notice about one-time or non-renewing payment.
  • Avoid language that promises automatic renewal unless the supported payment flow is confirmed.
  • The page should make the payment type clear before the user pays.

Example:

  • India billing notice: This purchase is treated as a one-time payment with no automatic renewal unless a supported renewal flow is shown.

Other Countries

When Country is not Canada or India:

  • Keep the billing address form normal.
  • Show a neutral note: Taxes, if any, are calculated during checkout or by Stripe.

10. Key User Flows

Flow A: Save Billing Address

  1. User opens Billing from the dashboard sidebar.
  2. Billing page opens inside the dashboard shell.
  3. User enters required billing address fields.
  4. User optionally enters company, phone, and tax number.
  5. User saves billing details.
  6. Page confirms the details were saved.

Flow B: Add Card After Subscription or Purchase

  1. User subscribes or purchases through Stripe.
  2. User returns to Billing.
  3. Payment method card shows safe card details, such as brand, last four digits, and expiration date.
  4. Page shows that card details are handled securely by Stripe.

Flow C: Update Payment Method

  1. User opens Billing.
  2. User clicks Update payment method.
  3. User enters card number, expiration date, security code, and name on card in the secure Stripe card form.
  4. Payment method updates.
  5. Page shows safe saved-card details only.

Flow D: Canada Tax Estimate

  1. User selects Canada as country.
  2. User selects province or territory.
  3. Billing page shows the estimated tax rate for that province or territory.
  4. User understands the final tax may be confirmed during checkout.

Flow E: India One-Time Payment Notice

  1. User selects India as country.
  2. Billing page shows the India payment notice.
  3. User understands that payment is one-time or non-renewing unless a supported renewal flow is clearly shown.

11. States and Edge Cases

Loading States

  • Loading billing profile.
  • Saving billing profile.
  • Loading payment method.
  • Updating payment method.
  • Loading tax estimate.

Empty States

  • No billing profile yet.
  • No payment method yet.
  • Country selected but state/province not selected.
  • No tax number entered.

Error States

  • Required billing fields are missing.
  • Country and state/province combination is invalid.
  • Postal code format is invalid.
  • Billing email format is invalid.
  • Payment method cannot load.
  • Payment method update fails.
  • Tax estimate cannot be shown.
  • Save fails.

Edge Cases

  • User has subscribed but no card details are available from Stripe.
  • User has a card that is expired.
  • User has a long company name.
  • User has a long address.
  • User switches country after selecting a province.
  • User selects Canada but does not choose a province or territory.
  • User selects India after previously seeing renewal language.
  • User is a business customer but leaves tax number blank.
  • User is a personal customer and does not need company or tax fields.

12. Accessibility and Usability

  • Every input must have a visible label.
  • Required fields must be clear without relying on color alone.
  • Optional fields should be labeled as optional.
  • Error messages should appear near the related field.
  • The user should be able to complete the form with a keyboard.
  • Tax notes should be readable and not hidden behind hover-only help.
  • Payment security message should be visible near the card area.
  • Card fields should clearly belong to Stripe's secure payment area.
  • Long addresses and company names should not break the layout.
  • The active Billing sidebar item should be announced as the current page.

13. Suggested UI Copy

Header

  • Billing
  • Manage your billing address, tax details, and payment method.
  • Save billing details

Billing Address

  • Billing address
  • Used for invoices, tax calculation, and billing communication.
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Billing email
  • Company name
  • Address
  • Address line 2
  • City
  • Country
  • State / province
  • ZIP / postal code
  • Phone number
  • Billing details saved.

Tax Details

  • Tax details
  • Tax details help MapThru prepare accurate invoices.
  • Tax number
  • Tax is estimated from your selected province or territory.
  • Taxes, if any, are calculated during checkout.

Payment Method

  • Payment method
  • Card information will appear after you subscribe or purchase through Stripe.
  • MapThru does not store your card details. Card information is handled securely by Stripe.
  • Card ending in [last four digits]
  • Add payment method
  • Update payment method

Country Notices

  • Canada tax note: Estimated tax: [rate].
  • India billing notice: This purchase is treated as a one-time payment with no automatic renewal unless a supported renewal flow is shown.

14. Acceptance Criteria

Layout and Style

  • Billing page uses the dashboard shell from src/app/dashboard/page.tsx.
  • Top MapThru nav is present.
  • Left sidebar is present on large screens.
  • Billing is the active sidebar item.
  • Main content uses rounded dashboard-style cards.
  • Right rail summarizes billing, payment, and tax status on wide screens.
  • Page does not use the old centered billing-card layout.

Billing Address

  • User can enter first name, last name, billing email, company name, address, city, country, state/province, ZIP/postal code, phone number, and tax number.
  • Required fields are clearly marked.
  • Optional fields are clearly optional.
  • User can save billing details.
  • User sees success after saving.
  • User sees helpful validation errors when required fields are missing.

Payment Method

  • Card information appears only after the user subscribes or purchases through Stripe.
  • User can see safe saved-card details only.
  • Full card number and security code are never shown as saved data.
  • Page clearly explains that MapThru does not store card details.
  • User can add or update payment method through a secure Stripe card area.

Canada Taxes

  • Selecting Canada makes province or territory important and required.
  • Selecting a Canadian province or territory shows the correct estimated tax rate.
  • Page explains that final tax may depend on final checkout and Stripe tax settings.

India Payment Behavior

  • Selecting India shows a one-time or no-renewal-payment notice.
  • Page avoids automatic-renewal language for India unless a supported renewal flow is clearly shown.

15. QA Scenarios

  1. User opens Billing from the sidebar and sees Billing active.
  2. User saves a complete billing address successfully.
  3. User tries to save without first name and sees a field error.
  4. User tries to save without billing email and sees a field error.
  5. User selects Canada and must choose a province or territory.
  6. User selects Ontario and sees 13% HST.
  7. User selects Nova Scotia and sees 14% HST.
  8. User selects Quebec and sees 14.975% combined tax.
  9. User selects India and sees the one-time or no-renewal-payment notice.
  10. User has not purchased yet and sees no payment method.
  11. User has purchased through Stripe and sees safe card details only.
  12. User updates payment method and sees a security message about Stripe.
  13. Long company name does not break the card layout.
  14. Keyboard-only user can complete the billing form.

16. Open Questions

Question Recommended default Owner
Should Billing email default to account email? Yes, prefill it but allow editing. Product
Should phone number be required? No, keep it optional. Product
Should tax number be required for companies? No, keep it optional but important. Product / Finance
Should address line 2 be included? Yes, optional, for suite/unit/building details. Product / Design
Should Canada taxes use only GST/HST or include PST/QST display too? Show combined visible tax estimate by province or territory. Product / Finance
Should India always use one-time payment? Treat India as one-time or non-renewing unless the supported renewal setup is confirmed. Product / Finance
Should payment method editing open Stripe-hosted billing portal or an embedded secure card area? Prefer the safest Stripe-managed experience. Product / Engineering

17. Risks

Risk Impact Mitigation
Users think MapThru stores card data. Trust and compliance concerns. Put the Stripe security note directly beside payment method controls.
Too many fields feel mandatory. Users abandon the form. Require only fields needed for billing, tax, or payment.
Canada tax rates become outdated. Incorrect tax expectation. Treat displayed rates as estimates and keep rates aligned with trusted tax settings.
India renewal language is unclear. Users may misunderstand payment terms. Show a plain one-time/no-renewal notice when India is selected.
Billing page does not match dashboard style. Product feels inconsistent. Reuse dashboard shell, sidebar, rounded cards, right rail, and muted helper text.
Saved card display exposes too much information. Security and compliance issue. Show only safe card summary details returned by Stripe.

18. Reference Notes

  • Canada tax rates are based on the Canada Revenue Agency GST/HST calculator and rates page, including the Nova Scotia HST decrease to 14% as of April 1, 2025.
  • Stripe guidance says low-risk integrations can securely collect and transmit payment information directly to Stripe without it passing through the business's servers. Stripe can return non-sensitive card details such as card type, last four digits, and expiration date.

19. Design Summary

The Billing page should be a dashboard-native billing settings page. It should collect billing address and tax details, show safe payment method information from Stripe, explain that MapThru does not store card data, and provide country-aware guidance for Canada taxes and India one-time or non-renewing payments. The user should immediately understand what information is required, what is optional, what is secure, and what payment rules apply to their country.

brainstorming.md - Subscription Plan Page

Branch: product-docs
Sources: User brief, src/app/dashboard/page.tsx, profile page brainstorming, billing page brainstorming, subscription pricing spreadsheet

RESULT

GitHub Branch: UI-UX-Create-subscription-plan

1. Shared Understanding

Goal

Create a Subscription Plan page where users can understand their current subscription status, compare Free, Basic, and Pro plans, choose the right subscription action, and buy add-ons for Publish Projects and AI Floor Scanner credits.

Product Intent

The page should help users answer four questions quickly:

  1. What plan am I currently on?
  2. What do Free, Basic, and Pro include?
  3. Should I subscribe, upgrade, or downgrade?
  4. What add-ons can I buy for publishing or AI Floor Scanner usage?

The page should feel like the dashboard and profile pages: calm, workspace-native, rounded, structured, and direct. It should not feel like a marketing landing page.

In Scope

  • Subscription status summary.
  • Free, Basic, and Pro plan price list.
  • Plan comparison details:
    • Plan name.
    • Price.
    • Publish project limit.
    • AI Floor Scanner credit amount.
    • Export to GeoJSON availability.
    • View details link to the pricing plan page.
    • Subscribe, Upgrade, or Downgrade button.
  • Add-on Publish price list:
    • Extra Publish Project.
    • Temporary Publish Pass.
    • Only visible when the user has an active subscription plan.
  • Add-on AI Floor Scanner Credit price list:
    • Always visible for subscribed and unsubscribed users.
  • Subscription status states:
    • Current subscription plan.
    • Renewal or expiration date.
    • Subscribed.
    • Pending unsubscribed.
    • Unsubscribed.
  • Non-technical design guidance for UI UX Pro Max.

Out of Scope

  • Full checkout flow.
  • Billing address editing.
  • Card management.
  • Invoice history.
  • Receipt downloads.
  • Tax calculation.
  • Team or organization subscription management.
  • Deep pricing-plan marketing page content.

2. Dashboard and Profile Style Source of Truth

The Subscription Plan page should use the same workspace shell and visual rhythm as the dashboard and profile page.

Shell Pattern

Use the same layout family:

  • Sticky MapThru top navigation.
  • Left sidebar on large screens.
  • Subscription Plan active in the sidebar.
  • Main content column.
  • Right rail on wide screens.
  • Soft ambient brand wash behind the page.
  • Wide workspace container.
  • Responsive stacking on smaller screens.

Visual Language

Preserve these style cues:

  • Rounded-xl and rounded-2xl surfaces.
  • Soft borders.
  • Semi-transparent card surfaces.
  • Muted helper text.
  • Small icon-led labels.
  • Primary color accents for the selected or current plan.
  • Amber treatment for upgrade prompts, expiring plans, or attention states.
  • Destructive or caution styling only for downgrade or unsubscribed states.
  • Gradient primary button for the strongest recommended action.
  • Compact headings and clean comparison cards.

What the Page Should Not Become

  • Not a hero landing page.
  • Not a dense spreadsheet copied into the UI.
  • Not a checkout page.
  • Not a modal-only experience.
  • Not a one-column wall of prices.

3. Recommended Page Direction

Recommended Approach: Account-Native Plan Management Page

Create a dedicated Subscription Plan page inside the dashboard shell:

  1. Top status summary explains the user's current subscription state.
  2. Three plan cards compare Free, Basic, and Pro.
  3. Add-on Publish section appears only for subscribed users.
  4. Add-on AI Floor Scanner Credit section always appears.
  5. Right rail summarizes current plan, renewal/expiration date, and recommended next action.

This approach is recommended because the page is both a comparison page and an account-management page. Users should see pricing clearly, but the first priority is helping them manage their current MapThru subscription.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative A: Full pricing table

This would show many details at once, but it may feel too dense inside the dashboard. Plan cards are easier to scan.

Alternative B: Checkout-first plan page

This would push users toward payment quickly, but it would hide important plan comparison and status context.

Alternative C: Split plans and add-ons into separate pages

This would reduce page length, but users need to understand plans and add-ons together because add-ons depend on subscription status.

4. Price Source of Truth

Pricing and limits come from the linked spreadsheet:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1O41UmDzbGDWQNm10k2uDIRaHPNRnP9k6HJ4Cbl9Ur1Y/edit?usp=sharing

Subscription Plans

Plan Price Draft projects Publish projects Extra publish project slots AI Floor Scanner Export to GeoJSON
Free $0 1 project 0 projects 0 slots 1 credit No
Basic $10/month or $100/year 5 projects 2 projects 3 slots 5 credits/month Yes
Pro $20/month or $200/year Unlimited 10 projects Unlimited 25 credits/month Yes

Additional plan features from the spreadsheet:

  • Share Published Project:
    • Free: No.
    • Basic: Yes.
    • Pro: Yes.
  • Embed Published Project:
    • Free: No.
    • Basic: Yes.
    • Pro: Yes.
  • Preview Project:
    • Free: Yes.
    • Basic: Yes.
    • Pro: Yes.
  • Level per Project:
    • Free: 1 level.
    • Basic: 3 levels.
    • Pro: Unlimited.
  • Object per Project:
    • Free: 100 objects.
    • Basic: 1,000 objects.
    • Pro: Unlimited.
  • Objects include walls, doors, windows, areas, safety annotations, and points.
  • Unused monthly included AI Floor Scanner credits should not accumulate forever.

Add-On Publish Prices

Add-on Price Use case
Extra Publish Project $5/month or $50/year For users who need more active published projects without upgrading their plan.
Temporary Publish Pass $8/month or $80/year For events, exhibitions, temporary venues, demos, short campaigns, or one-time public sharing.

Add-On AI Floor Scanner Credit Prices

Add-on Price Note
5 AI Floor Scanner Credits $9 Does not combine with monthly credit accumulation.
15 AI Floor Scanner Credits $24 Does not combine with monthly credit accumulation.
50 AI Floor Scanner Credits $69 Does not combine with monthly credit accumulation.
150 AI Floor Scanner Credits $179 Does not combine with monthly credit accumulation.

5. Page Layout

Header Area

Purpose: Introduce the page and show the user's subscription context.

Suggested content:

  • Small context label: Subscription plan
  • Main title: Plans and add-ons
  • Supporting text: Compare plans, manage your subscription, and add more publishing or AI scanner capacity.
  • Optional compact status chip: Current plan: Free, Basic, or Pro.

Subscription Status Summary

Place near the top, before the price cards.

The summary should show:

  • Current subscription plan.
  • Subscription status.
  • Renewal date or expiration date.
  • Pending unsubscribed state when cancellation is scheduled.
  • Unsubscribed state when the user no longer has an active plan.

Suggested status labels:

  • Subscribed.
  • Pending unsubscribe.
  • Unsubscribed.
  • Free plan.

Suggested examples:

  • Current plan: Basic.

  • Status: Subscribed.

  • Renews on: August 1, 2026.

  • Current plan: Pro.

  • Status: Pending unsubscribe.

  • Access ends on: August 1, 2026.

  • Current plan: Free.

  • Status: Unsubscribed.

  • No renewal date.

Plan Cards Section

Show Free, Basic, and Pro as three cards in one responsive section.

Each card should include:

  • Plan name.
  • Price.
  • Publish project limit.
  • AI Floor Scanner amount.
  • Export to GeoJSON availability.
  • View details link.
  • Plan action button.

Recommended card emphasis:

  • Current plan card gets a clear "Current plan" badge.
  • Pro can receive a subtle "Best for teams" or "Most capacity" badge if product wants a recommendation.
  • Free should stay calm and not look like an error.
  • Downgrade action should look less dominant than Subscribe or Upgrade.

Add-On Publish Section

Only show this section if the user has an active subscribed plan.

Show:

  • Extra Publish Project.
  • Temporary Publish Pass.
  • Price.
  • Short use case.
  • Buy add-on button.

If the user is Free or unsubscribed, hide this section or replace it with a small note in the plan cards explaining that publish add-ons become available after subscribing.

Add-On AI Floor Scanner Credit Section

Always show this section.

Show:

  • 5 credits for $9.
  • 15 credits for $24.
  • 50 credits for $69.
  • 150 credits for $179.
  • Note that these add-on credits do not combine with monthly credit accumulation.
  • Buy credits button on each option.

Right Rail

On wide screens, use a right rail for:

  • Current subscription status.
  • Renewal or access end date.
  • Current publish usage, if available.
  • Current AI Floor Scanner credit balance, if available.
  • Short note about monthly included credits.
  • Primary recommended action:
    • Subscribe when user is Free.
    • Upgrade when user is Basic.
    • Manage plan when user is Pro.

6. Plan Action Button Rules

The plan action button has three modes.

Subscribe

Use when the user has not subscribed yet.

Example:

  • User is on Free or unsubscribed.
  • Basic card button: Subscribe.
  • Pro card button: Subscribe.

Upgrade

Use when the target plan is higher than the user's current plan.

Examples:

  • Current plan is Free, target plan is Basic or Pro: Upgrade or Subscribe depending on product language.
  • Current plan is Basic, target plan is Pro: Upgrade.

Recommended product language:

  • Use Subscribe for users with no paid plan.
  • Use Upgrade for paid users moving to a higher plan.

Downgrade

Use when the target plan is lower than the user's current paid plan.

Examples:

  • Current plan is Pro, target plan is Basic: Downgrade.
  • Current plan is Pro or Basic, target plan is Free: Downgrade.

Downgrade should be visually quieter than Upgrade. It should be clear, but not styled as the recommended action.

Current Plan

The current plan card should not show Subscribe, Upgrade, or Downgrade.

Recommended button or label:

  • Current plan.
  • Manage plan.

Use "Manage plan" if the user can change renewal or cancellation settings from this page.

7. Subscription Status States

Subscribed

Meaning:

  • User has an active paid plan.

Display:

  • Current plan.
  • Status: Subscribed.
  • Renewal date.
  • Active plan badge.

Pending Unsubscribed

Meaning:

  • User has canceled renewal, but still has access until the end date.

Display:

  • Current plan.
  • Status: Pending unsubscribe.
  • Access ends on date.
  • Keep plan benefits visible until expiration.
  • Offer a "Resume subscription" or "Keep plan" action if supported.

Unsubscribed

Meaning:

  • User does not have an active paid plan.

Display:

  • Current plan: Free.
  • Status: Unsubscribed.
  • No renewal date.
  • Subscribe buttons on paid plans.
  • Hide add-on Publish section.
  • Keep AI Floor Scanner credit add-ons visible.

Free Plan

Meaning:

  • User is using free access without a paid subscription.

Display:

  • Current plan: Free.
  • Free benefits.
  • Subscribe buttons on Basic and Pro.
  • No add-on Publish section.

8. UI/UX Master Data For UI UX Pro Max

Navigation Pattern

Pattern: Dashboard shell with left sidebar, main content, and right rail.
Active navigation item: Subscription Plan.
Entry points: Dashboard sidebar, profile page subscription card, billing page, upgrade prompt.
Exit points: Pricing plan details page, checkout, billing page, dashboard.

Screen Inventory

Screen ID Screen name Navigation type Entry from Exits to
S-01 Subscription Plan Sidebar page Dashboard, Profile, Billing, Upgrade prompt Pricing details, Checkout, Billing, Dashboard

S-01: Subscription Plan

  • Purpose: Let users compare subscription plans, understand current status, and buy plan or add-on capacity.
  • Key elements:
    • Dashboard shell.
    • Subscription status summary.
    • Free, Basic, and Pro plan cards.
    • Plan action buttons.
    • Add-On Publish section.
    • Add-On AI Floor Scanner Credit section.
    • Right rail summary.
  • Primary action:
    • Subscribe, Upgrade, or Manage plan based on user state.
  • Required states:
    • Default.
    • Loading.
    • Free/unsubscribed.
    • Subscribed.
    • Pending unsubscribe.
    • Error.
    • Add-on unavailable.
    • Add-on available.
  • Design implications:
    • The current plan must be instantly recognizable.
    • Paid plan options should be easy to compare without reading dense tables.
    • Add-ons should feel secondary to the main plans but still purchasable.
    • AI Floor Scanner credits are always visible because both free and paid users can buy them.

New Components To Design

Component Purpose
Subscription status summary Shows plan, status, renewal or expiration date.
Plan comparison card Shows each plan's price, key limits, details link, and action.
Plan action button Supports Subscribe, Upgrade, Downgrade, Current plan, and Manage plan states.
Add-on publish card Shows publish add-ons available only to subscribed users.
Add-on AI credit card Shows credit bundles available to all users.
Subscription right rail summary Shows compact current plan, usage, dates, and next action.

Interaction And Motion

Interaction Behavior
Select plan action Button shows working state and routes user to checkout or plan-management flow.
View details Opens pricing plan page for that plan.
Buy publish add-on Starts add-on purchase flow for subscribed users.
Buy AI credits Starts credit purchase flow for all users.
Downgrade Uses calmer button treatment and may require confirmation.
Pending unsubscribe Shows access-end date and optionally offers resume action.

Accessibility Requirements

  • Plan cards must have clear headings.
  • Prices must be readable and not only communicated by color.
  • Current plan must be announced as text, not only highlighted visually.
  • Buttons must clearly say Subscribe, Upgrade, Downgrade, Manage plan, or Current plan.
  • Add-on availability must be explained in text.
  • The page must be usable by keyboard.
  • Responsive layout must keep plan cards readable on small screens.

9. Suggested UI Copy

Header

  • Plans and add-ons
  • Compare plans, manage your subscription, and add more publishing or AI scanner capacity.

Subscription Status

  • Current plan
  • Status
  • Renews on
  • Access ends on
  • Subscribed
  • Pending unsubscribe
  • Unsubscribed
  • Free plan

Plan Cards

  • Free
  • Basic
  • Pro
  • Current plan
  • Subscribe
  • Upgrade
  • Downgrade
  • Manage plan
  • View details
  • Export to GeoJSON
  • Publish projects
  • AI Floor Scanner

Add-On Publish

  • Add-on Publish
  • Extra Publish Project
  • Temporary Publish Pass
  • Available for subscribed users.
  • Buy add-on

Add-On AI Credits

  • AI Floor Scanner credits
  • Add credits when you need more scans.
  • These add-on credits do not combine with monthly credit accumulation.
  • Buy credits

Empty Or Locked States

  • Publish add-ons are available after you subscribe to a paid plan.
  • AI Floor Scanner credits are available with or without a subscription.
  • We could not load your subscription details. Please try again.

10. Key User Flows

Flow A: Free User Subscribes

  1. User opens Subscription Plan from the sidebar.
  2. Status summary shows Free plan or Unsubscribed.
  3. User compares Free, Basic, and Pro cards.
  4. User clicks Subscribe on Basic or Pro.
  5. User moves to checkout or subscription flow.

Flow B: Basic User Upgrades To Pro

  1. User opens Subscription Plan.
  2. Status summary shows Basic and renewal date.
  3. Basic card is marked Current plan.
  4. Pro card shows Upgrade.
  5. User clicks Upgrade.

Flow C: Pro User Downgrades

  1. User opens Subscription Plan.
  2. Status summary shows Pro and renewal date.
  3. Basic or Free card shows Downgrade.
  4. User clicks Downgrade.
  5. Page clearly warns or confirms the downgrade if required.

Flow D: Subscribed User Buys Publish Add-On

  1. User opens Subscription Plan while subscribed.
  2. Add-On Publish section is visible.
  3. User chooses Extra Publish Project or Temporary Publish Pass.
  4. User clicks Buy add-on.

Flow E: Any User Buys AI Floor Scanner Credits

  1. User opens Subscription Plan.
  2. AI Floor Scanner Credit section is visible.
  3. User chooses 5, 15, 50, or 150 credits.
  4. User clicks Buy credits.

Flow F: Pending Unsubscribe User Reviews Access

  1. User opens Subscription Plan.
  2. Status summary shows Pending unsubscribe.
  3. Page shows access end date.
  4. User can decide whether to resume, subscribe again, or wait until expiration.

11. States And Edge Cases

Loading States

  • Loading subscription status.
  • Loading plan prices.
  • Starting subscription.
  • Starting upgrade.
  • Starting downgrade.
  • Buying add-on.
  • Loading add-on availability.

Empty States

  • No paid subscription.
  • No renewal date.
  • No publish add-ons available because user is not subscribed.
  • No AI credit balance available.

Error States

  • Subscription status cannot load.
  • Pricing cannot load.
  • Checkout cannot start.
  • Upgrade cannot start.
  • Downgrade cannot start.
  • Add-on purchase cannot start.

Edge Cases

  • User is Free but has purchased AI credits.
  • User is pending unsubscribe but still has plan benefits until expiration.
  • User is Pro and cannot upgrade further.
  • User is Free and cannot downgrade.
  • User has Basic but publish add-ons are unavailable due to payment issue.
  • User has expired subscription but still sees old plan name.
  • Spreadsheet pricing changes and UI needs updated values.

12. Acceptance Criteria

Layout And Style

  • Subscription Plan page uses the same dashboard shell as src/app/dashboard/page.tsx.
  • Top MapThru navigation is present.
  • Left sidebar is present on large screens.

1. Shared Understanding

Goal

Create an Invoice page where users can view their invoice history in a clear table, sorted by the latest date first, with status tabs for All, Paid, Pending, and Overdue. Each invoice row should show date, product, type, amount, status, and a download button.

Product Intent

The page should help users quickly answer:

  1. What invoices do I have?
  2. Which invoices are paid, pending, or overdue?
  3. What product or purchase does each invoice belong to?
  4. Can I download the invoice immediately?

The page should feel like the dashboard, profile, billing, and subscription pages: workspace-native, calm, rounded, table-focused, and easy to scan.

In Scope

  • Invoice list table.
  • Default sorting by latest date first.
  • Invoice status tabs:
    • All.
    • Paid.
    • Pending.
    • Overdue.
  • Counter inside each status tab, matching the dashboard tab-counter pattern.
  • Table columns:
    • Date.
    • Product.
    • Type.
    • Amount.
    • Status.
    • Download.
  • Invoice type values:
    • Subscription.
    • Extra Publish.
    • Publish Pass.
    • AI Credits.
  • Invoice status values:
    • Paid.
    • Pending.
    • Overdue.
  • Download button for each row.
  • Empty, loading, filtered-empty, and error states.
  • Non-technical UI/UX data source for Claude's UI UX Pro Max skill.

Out of Scope

  • Creating invoices.
  • Editing invoice data.
  • Payment retry flow.
  • Refund management.
  • Tax detail editing.
  • Billing address editing.
  • Card management.
  • Full invoice PDF design.
  • Deep financial reporting.

2. Dashboard Style Source of Truth

The Invoice page should use the same workspace shell and visual rhythm as the dashboard and account pages.

Shell Pattern

Use the same layout family:

  • Sticky MapThru top navigation.
  • Left sidebar on large screens.
  • Invoice active in the sidebar.
  • Main content column.
  • Optional right rail on wide screens.
  • Soft ambient brand wash behind the page.
  • Wide workspace container.
  • Responsive stacking on smaller screens.

Visual Language

Preserve these dashboard cues:

  • Rounded-xl and rounded-2xl surfaces.
  • Soft borders.
  • Semi-transparent card or table container.
  • Muted helper text.
  • Compact headings.
  • Tab list with counters, matching the dashboard project-status filter tabs.
  • Primary color for the active tab.
  • Green or success treatment for Paid.
  • Amber treatment for Pending.
  • Destructive or caution treatment for Overdue.
  • Icon button or compact button for Download.

What The Page Should Not Become

  • Not a marketing page.
  • Not a checkout page.
  • Not a dense accounting dashboard.
  • Not a card grid when a table is clearer.
  • Not a full invoice preview page.

3. Recommended Page Direction

Recommended Approach: Table-First Invoice History Page

Create a dedicated Invoice page inside the dashboard shell:

  1. Header introduces invoice history.
  2. A compact summary shows total invoices and key counts.
  3. Status tabs filter the table by All, Paid, Pending, and Overdue.
  4. Invoice table lists invoices sorted by newest date first.
  5. Each row has a Download button.
  6. Right rail can summarize invoice status counts or billing links on wide screens.

This is recommended because invoice history is naturally tabular. Users need to scan dates, amounts, status, and download actions quickly.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative A: Invoice cards

Cards would be more visual, but they make it harder to compare dates, amounts, and statuses across many invoices.

Alternative B: Separate pages for each invoice status

Separate pages would add navigation weight. Status tabs are faster and match the dashboard pattern.

Alternative C: Full financial dashboard

This would be too heavy for the current goal. Users only need a clean invoice list and downloads.

4. Page Layout

Header Area

Purpose: Explain the page and show invoice context.

Suggested content:

  • Small context label: Billing history.
  • Main title: Invoices.
  • Supporting text: View and download your MapThru invoices.
  • Optional summary line: [Total] invoices, [Paid] paid, [Pending] pending, [Overdue] overdue.

Style:

  • Use the same title scale and gradient treatment as the dashboard account pages.
  • Keep the header compact.
  • Do not create a hero section.

Main Content

Recommended order:

  1. Header.
  2. Optional compact invoice summary.
  3. Status tabs with counters.
  4. Invoice table.
  5. Empty or error state when needed.

Right Rail

On wide screens, the right rail can show:

  • Invoice summary counts.
  • Last invoice date.
  • Outstanding amount if there are pending or overdue invoices.
  • Link to Billing.
  • Link to Subscription Plan.

The right rail should support the table, not duplicate every row.

5. Invoice Table

Purpose

Give users a clear list of invoices with the most recent invoice first.

Default Sort

  • Sort by date, newest first.
  • Latest invoice should appear at the top.
  • If two invoices share the same date, show the newest created invoice first if available.

Columns

Column Purpose Notes
Date Shows when the invoice was created or issued. Use a readable date format.
Product Shows what was purchased. Examples: Basic Plan, Pro Plan, Extra Publish Project, AI Floor Scanner Credits.
Type Shows purchase category. Subscription, Extra Publish, Publish Pass, AI Credits.
Amount Shows invoice total. Include currency.
Status Shows invoice state. Paid, Pending, Overdue.
Download Lets user download invoice. Button should be compact and clear.

Row Behavior

  • Paid rows should feel resolved and calm.
  • Pending rows should feel noticeable but not alarming.
  • Overdue rows should be easy to identify.
  • Download button should be available when a file exists.
  • If download is unavailable, show a disabled button or short unavailable message.

Suggested Row Copy

  • Download.
  • Downloading...
  • Unavailable.
  • Paid.
  • Pending.
  • Overdue.

6. Status Tabs With Counters

Purpose

Let users filter invoice data quickly by status and understand how many invoices are in each status.

Tabs

Tab Meaning
All Shows every invoice.
Paid Shows paid invoices only.
Pending Shows pending invoices only.
Overdue Shows overdue invoices only.

Counter Behavior

  • Each tab shows a small counter.
  • Counter style should match the dashboard's project status tabs.
  • Active tab should use the dashboard active-tab treatment.
  • Inactive tabs should stay muted but readable.

Example:

  • All 24
  • Paid 20
  • Pending 3
  • Overdue 1

Filtering Behavior

  • Selecting a tab filters the table.
  • The selected tab remains visually active.
  • If a selected tab has no invoices, show a filtered-empty state.
  • Filters should not change the default sort order; the filtered list still shows newest first.

7. Invoice Type Treatment

Supported Types

  • Subscription.
  • Extra Publish.
  • Publish Pass.
  • AI Credits.

Display Guidance

  • Use concise labels in the Type column.
  • Product column should give the specific product name.
  • Type column should give the category.

Examples:

Product Type
Pro Plan Monthly Subscription
Extra Publish Project Extra Publish
Temporary Publish Pass Publish Pass
50 AI Floor Scanner Credits AI Credits

Visual Treatment

  • Type labels can use subtle badges.
  • Avoid too many bright colors.
  • Status should carry more visual weight than type.

8. Status Treatment

Paid

Meaning:

  • Invoice has been paid.

Display:

  • Use calm success treatment.
  • Label: Paid.

Pending

Meaning:

  • Invoice is waiting for payment or processing.

Display:

  • Use amber or attention treatment.
  • Label: Pending.

Overdue

Meaning:

  • Invoice is past its payment due date.

Display:

  • Use caution or destructive-adjacent treatment.
  • Label: Overdue.
  • Make overdue rows easy to find without making the whole page feel alarming.
